newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Northland Port warns of lower H1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Northland Port warns of lower H1 earnings.

text.p: Northland Port Corporation (NZ) Ltd said on Friday it was expecting earnings to fall below forecast in the six months to March 31, and said they were likely to be some 30 percent lower than the year-ago figure for the same period of NZ$4.25 million.
"While corrective actions are being taken, benefits are not expected to flow through until the second half," a statement quoted company chairman Jim Hardie as saying.
Half year results are due to be announced in mid-May and Hardie said the company expected to maintain its interim dividend at 2.75 cents per share.
The port operator named two factors as contributing to the downturn, namely -
* falling engineering workload, made worse by an industrial dispute at Whangarei shipyards,
* higher than normal maintenance in marine transport business, which otherwise had a normal half year, compared to an exceptionally busy year-ago period.
